name: Grand Theft Auto V (story mode only)
warning: Only use the merged copy in Story Mode. Modded files in GTA Online can get your account banned.

themes.name: Schedule I x Hood Warfare: business, gangs and guns
themes.description: Los Santos as Schedule I's business and Hood Warfare's gang war: buy labs and farms, cook and grow product, sell it on the street, hire workers and dealers, and take turf from GTA V's own gangs in timed turf wars, with police heat and raids. Built by Frankenstein's own GTA V script from GTA V's own people, places and guns; nothing is copied from Schedule I or Hood Warfare. Story mode only, offline.

slots.name: Labs, farms and production
slots.builtin: Frankenstein's own GTA V script: five properties to buy (Strawberry stash house, Grapeseed farm, Sandy Shores lab, La Mesa gun workshop, Elysian Island warehouse). Buy supplies, start a batch (weed, meth, coke or gun crates) and collect it when it's ready. Specialist workers: a botanist, chemist or gunsmith who runs the place, a handler who packs 25% more, and a cleaner who halves the heat and keeps raids off it. Rest at any property you own (sleep 6 hours) and stock up on snacks there. F5 (or hold D-pad left) opens the empire menu with waypoints.

slots.name: Story and Creative modes
slots.builtin: Story plays like Schedule I, in 18 objectives with phone calls from Uncle Ray: your uncle's stash house in Strawberry, your first weed, a first customer, mixing, the bigger properties, workers, a turf war, your own crew, La Sombra's cartel, guns and coke, up to Kingpin. Ranks from Street Rat to Kingpin unlock each step, and big moments get a cutscene. Creative is for testing: everything owned and unlocked, unlimited money and supplies, 30-second batches, heat and survival off unless you turn them on, and test tools in the F5 menu (product, customers, crew, cartel, survival, raids, turf wars, cutscenes). Each mode keeps its own saves and empire; switch in game from the F5 menu (works on a controller) or Shift+F10.

slots.name: Mixing and effects
slots.builtin: Like Schedule I's mixing: at a property, add up to three ingredients to a product (cucumber, banana, energy drink, paracetamol, motor oil, chili, battery, glow sticks, gasoline). Each one gives an effect (Refreshing, Calming, Energizing, Spicy, Glowing and so on) that raises the street price, changes how hooked people get and costs a little more each batch.

slots.name: Customers and addiction
slots.builtin: 14 named customers across five areas that open as you rank up. Give someone a free sample (better odds when your mix has the effect they like); once they're hooked they text you orders every in-game hour, bigger and better paid the more hooked they are. F5 > Customers lists them with waypoints.

slots.name: Street dealing and dealers
slots.builtin: Walk up to someone and press E (D-pad right) to offer product; the price is better on your own turf, and some buyers are undercover cops. Dealers you hire sell your stock every in-game hour on the turf you hold.

slots.name: Gangs and turf wars
slots.builtin: GTA V's own gangs hold their real neighbourhoods (Families, Ballas, Vagos, Aztecas, Marabunta, The Lost, Kkangpae). Hold E (D-pad right) in a gang's zone to start a four-minute turf war against armed crews; win it and the zone is yours and pays every hour. Gangs try to take turf back, or you can buy a truce.

slots.name: Your crew
slots.builtin: From Bagman you hire crew members ($3,000 each, $150 an hour), call them to follow you and fight, and buy them better gear (Street to Elite). Left at home they guard your turf, so gangs often fail to take it back. Crew who die are gone.

slots.name: La Sombra (cartel)
slots.builtin: Once you're big enough, the La Sombra cartel wants a meeting at the Sandy Shores airfield. Pay them 15% and they keep the gangs off your turf, or tell them to get lost: then they ambush you, and you hit their three stashes and finally their boss at a ranch in the hills. You can stop paying later from the F5 menu.

slots.name: Police heat and raids
slots.builtin: Dealing and fighting raise heat; high heat brings police raids on your labs and a wanted level. Heat cools off over time.

slots.name: Hood Warfare guns
slots.builtin: The La Mesa gun workshop makes gun crates you sell to GTA V's gangs (the better your relations, the better they pay). F5 > Arsenal buys weapon kits that unlock by rank (Street, Corner, Soldier, Heavy) and body armour. These are GTA V's own guns; Hood Warfare's own gun models aren't built. Weapon mods can add more (picks below).

slots.name: Vehicles
slots.builtin: F5 > Vehicles: a garage of 13 GTA V cars and bikes that unlock by rank, from a Sanchez and lowriders to an armoured Kuruma, an Insurgent and a T20. Buy once, call it to you any time, upgrade engine, brakes, gearbox, suspension and armour, and paint it purple, black or gold. These are GTA V's own models (car mods can add more).

slots.name: Survival
slots.builtin: Outward-style needs in Story: hunger, thirst and energy bars on the HUD. Eat and drink from the F5 menu (snacks and drinks from your properties) or at GTA V's vending machines and food stands (E). Empty bars hurt you and stop you sprinting; no energy makes you stumble, so rest at a property. Off in Creative unless you turn it on.

slots.name: Gang Beasts ragdoll
slots.builtin: Frankenstein's ragdoll script on GTA V's own physics: J (double-tap D-pad down) flops you over, punches and melee hits send people flying, and sprinting into someone knocks them over. Shift+J turns the launches off. Grabbing and climbing like Gang Beasts aren't built.

slots.name: Cinematic look
slots.builtin: Frankenstein's GTA V script lays one of GTA V's own film filters over the game, stronger on the Cinematic graphics setting and off on Performance, and the F5 menu's Look page picks another filter or sets golden hour or night. The map shows every property with its rank and price and each gang's turf as a coloured ring, like the empire map. For the photoreal light of the concept art, a graphics mod (NaturalVision, QuantV) goes on top (picks below).

themes.name: Minecraft style: blocks, skins and creatures
themes.description: Gives Los Santos a Minecraft look: Steve and Alex player models, Minecraft creatures, blocky textures and build mods. No Minecraft files are copied.

multiplayer: GTA V story mode is single-player, so mods can't add friends to it. To play together, one of you runs a private FiveM server (the official community multiplayer for GTA V) and everyone connects to the host's party IP shown here. Your merge's script mods won't carry over to FiveM.

sandbox.native: Script Hook V comes with Native Trainer: press F4 in game for god mode, money, vehicles, weapons and teleports. Menyoo (F8) spawns any weapon or vehicle by name, add-on cars included.
sandbox.note: Story Mode only: creative merges always start offline.

slots.name: Menyoo (spawn any weapon, vehicle, ped or object)
